screens.title: Languages
screens.summary: The café's languages and its own words. Every screen is in English, Arabic and Kurdish. Here you add another language and give any phrase the café's own words: a whole new language, or a better word for the Arabic or Kurdish.
screens.get_there: Settings → Languages → “Open Languages →”. The link “Settings” above the heading goes back.

who.owner: add, rename, take out of use or bring back a language; give or clear words; download and upload CSV Not: remove or rename English, Arabic or Kurdish
who.general_manager: the same as the owner Not: the same
who.everyone else: nothing here Not: open the screen: they are sent to their own start screen

what_if.case: A Kurdish word on the till is wrong
what_if.do: Choose کوردی, search the English, type the better word in its box, Save.

what_if.case: We hired staff who read Turkish
what_if.do: Add a language: code tr, name Türkçe, Left to right. Download CSV, have it translated, Upload CSV, check and Save.

what_if.case: A saved word broke a sentence
what_if.do: Empty that box and Save: the built-in words (or English) come back.

tips: Search the English exactly as the screen shows it.
Use “Phrases with no words yet” to finish a new language.
Saved words are used on every screen at once; someone with a screen already open sees them when it is loaded again.

screens.title: Start of Day
screens.summary: The morning, step by step, before the doors open: the drawer opened and counted (done right here), everyone due in clocked in, what to make, deliveries due, nothing low without an order, and the red alerts answered. Then the day ahead. It records nothing by itself except opening the drawer.
screens.get_there: Menu → Operations → Start of Day (for the owner and general manager it is under More). Also: Dashboard, 4:00 to 11:59, “Opening up? The start of the day, step by step”; Find anything → “Start of Day”.

who.owner: every step, the day ahead, open the drawer with a float from the safe, and see what the drawer should hold
who.general_manager: the same as the owner
who.branch_manager: every step and open the drawer with a float from the safe Not: see what an open drawer should hold (needs cash.view_expected)
who.cashier: nothing here Not: open the screen (needs day.close): they are sent to their own start screen
who.barista: nothing here Not: open the screen (needs day.close): they are sent to their own start screen
who.inventory_counter: nothing here Not: open the screen (needs day.close): they are sent to their own start screen
who.purchasing: nothing here Not: open the screen (needs day.close): they are sent to their own start screen
who.accountant: nothing here Not: open the screen (needs day.close): they are sent to their own start screen
who.auditor: nothing here Not: open the screen (needs day.close): they are sent to their own start screen

what_if.case: The opening count differs from last night's close
what_if.do: Count again. If it still differs, open anyway: the difference is recorded (6300 Cash over / short) and the manager sees it on Sales → sessions.

what_if.case: The drawer needs change
what_if.do: A manager types the float in “Cash put in from the safe now (optional)” while opening.

what_if.case: A barista is late
what_if.do: Their name shows under the people step; they clock in on the till when they arrive. A manager corrects hours on Staff.

what_if.case: A delivery is late
what_if.do: It stays in Deliveries due with its date; call the supplier, receive it on Purchasing when it comes.

tips: Work top to bottom; the page ticks each step by itself when you come back.
The drawer step is done right on this page.
Try the printer on Test your devices before the first customer.

screens.title: End of Day
screens.summary: The close, step by step: bills paid, everyone clocked out, drawers closed and counted (done right here), losses approved, card and platform money, and red alerts answered. Then the day in numbers, to print or keep as a PDF, and a slip for the receipt printer.
screens.get_there: Menu → Operations → End of Day (for the owner and general manager under More). Also: Dashboard, from 16:00 to 03:59, “Closing up? The end of the day, step by step”; Find anything → “End of Day”.

who.owner: every step, the day in numbers, close or hand over the drawer, close someone else's drawer, see what it should hold, print
who.general_manager: the same as the owner
who.branch_manager: every step, the day in numbers, close or hand over, close someone else's drawer, print Not: see what an open drawer should hold before counting
who.cashier: nothing here Not: open the screen (needs day.close): they are sent to their own start screen
who.barista: nothing here Not: open the screen (needs day.close): they are sent to their own start screen
who.inventory_counter: nothing here Not: open the screen (needs day.close): they are sent to their own start screen
who.purchasing: nothing here Not: open the screen (needs day.close): they are sent to their own start screen
who.accountant: nothing here Not: open the screen (needs day.close): they are sent to their own start screen
who.auditor: nothing here Not: open the screen (needs day.close): they are sent to their own start screen

what_if.case: A cashier went home with the drawer open
what_if.do: In the drawer step press “Close it for them”, write why, count if you can (or leave it empty), and press the button.

what_if.case: The count is short
what_if.do: Count again before closing. If still short, close: the difference is recorded (6300 Cash over / short) and shows on the slip and on Sales → sessions.

what_if.case: A table did not pay
what_if.do: Leave the bill open: it is paid in the next session. If it will never be paid, a manager cancels it on the till with the reason.

what_if.case: Card total differs from the terminal
what_if.do: Check the card sales on Orders for today, and settle on Sales → Card Takings when the bank pays.

tips: Print the slip for the till and keep it with the cash, signed.
The page can be printed or saved as a PDF to keep.
Each step's button goes straight to where its work is done.

screens.title: Today — your jobs for the day
screens.summary: Where everyone starts after signing in: only today's jobs for your role, in the order of the day, each with one button to where it is done, and ticked once done. A cashier sees the drawer; a counter, the count waiting; a manager, the start of the day, approvals, deliveries and red alerts; the accountant, bills due, the bank and the books.
screens.get_there: Sign in: you land here (unless you chose another first screen on My account). Also: Menu → Today, the first entry.

who.owner: See and do today's jobs of their role.
who.general_manager: See and do today's jobs of their role.
who.branch_manager: See and do today's jobs of their role.
who.cashier: See and do today's jobs of their role.
who.barista: See and do today's jobs of their role.
who.inventory_counter: See and do today's jobs of their role.
who.purchasing: See and do today's jobs of their role.
who.accountant: See and do today's jobs of their role.
who.auditor: See and do today's jobs of their role.

what_if.case: A job you expected is not there
what_if.do: Today shows only what your role does. If it should be yours, ask the owner to check your role on Settings → People and roles.

what_if.case: It says “All done for now”
what_if.do: Nothing is waiting for you: carry on with your work, or check back later.

what_if.case: You are new
what_if.do: Press “Start practising” on the card at the top: you practise in a café of your own first, and nothing there is real.

tips: Each job's one button goes straight to where it is done.
To do comes first, then what waits on someone else, then later, then done.

screens.title: Practice — your work, with pretend money and stock
screens.summary: Practise your work in a practice café of your own: the same screens, a small menu (espresso, latte, croissant, water), stock, a supplier, two tables and two practice colleagues. Nothing done there reaches the café's books. Your role's tasks are listed in order, each ticked once you have done it in practice; when all are ticked you are ready. For whoever keeps the staff, the team's practice: each person's tasks done, and who is ready.
screens.get_there: My account → Practise first; the card at the top of Today; or the PRACTICE banner's “Your practice tasks” while practising.

who.owner: Practise their own role's tasks. See the team's practice.
who.general_manager: Practise their own role's tasks. See the team's practice.
who.branch_manager: Practise their own role's tasks. See the team's practice.

what_if.case: You are not sure whether you are practising
what_if.do: Look at the top: while practising, a striped PRACTICE banner is on every screen. With no banner, everything is real.

what_if.case: You want to start over
what_if.do: Press “Start again from the first day”: a fresh practice café; what you ticked stays ticked.

what_if.case: It says “Practice has ended”
what_if.do: Press “Back to the café”, then start practising again when you want.

what_if.case: A task is not ticked after you did it
what_if.do: Open Practice again: ticks are read from what you did. Check it matches the task (for example two small lattes, by card).

tips: Press “Stop practising” on the banner to go back to the real café.
Try everything in practice, including mistakes: nothing there is real.

screens.title: Production
screens.summary: Where the kitchen records what it makes in batches (gelato, a base, syrup, dough): the day's plan of what to make, recording a batch, the batches in stock with their use-by, labels for the pans, and marking down what must be sold today.
screens.get_there: Menu → Operations → Production. A barista starts here after signing in. Also: Getting set up's link (/production#new-recipe) opens the add-recipe panel; a 'Record these' link in the plan opens the form filled in.

who.owner: everything here: see costs and stock, record batches (also made earlier), cancel a batch, change a use-by, add and change recipes, mark down
who.general_manager: the same as the owner
who.branch_manager: see costs, record batches (also made earlier), cancel a batch, change a use-by, mark down Not: add or change recipes (needs recipe.edit)
who.barista: record batches, use the plan, print labels, mark down Not: see any cost or stock on hand, record a batch made earlier, cancel a batch, change a use-by, change recipes
who.purchasing: look: the plan, costs, batches, lots Not: record a batch, mark down, change anything
who.accountant: look: the plan, costs, batches, lots Not: record or change anything; the 'Sell it before it goes' card is not shown
who.auditor: look: the plan, costs, batches, lots Not: record or change anything; the 'Sell it before it goes' card is not shown
who.cashier: nothing Not: open the screen: they are sent to their own start screen
who.inventory_counter: nothing Not: open the screen: they are sent to their own start screen

what_if.case: The batch came out lighter than the recipe says
what_if.do: Type what you weighed in 'What came out (optional)' with its unit. The preview shows '— {diff} less than the recipe's {planned}'. Record it: stock gets what really came out, at the full cost of the ingredients.

what_if.case: I made it this morning before opening and forgot to record it
what_if.do: A manager ticks 'Made earlier: yesterday or today, recorded now', gives the time and why, and records it. Not possible if a count of its items was approved after that time, or before yesterday.

what_if.case: An ingredient shows 'only … in stock'
what_if.do: Usually a delivery is not entered. Enter it on Purchasing first. If the item's rule allows it, a manager can approve using more with their PIN; if it refuses, record the delivery or count it first.

what_if.case: A batch was recorded twice by mistake
what_if.do: A manager presses 'Cancel…' on the second one in Batches, types 'recorded twice', and 'Cancel the batch'. If some of it was already sold or used, record the rest as a loss on Inventory instead.

what_if.case: A batch went soft and must be sold today
what_if.do: A manager uses 'Change the use-by…' in In stock by batch, gives today's time and the reason. It then appears under 'Sell it before it goes', where it can be marked down.

what_if.case: Ice cream from today's batch will not sell before closing
what_if.do: In 'Sell it before it goes', press the suggested '{percent}% off' button. The till sells it cheaper until the day ends. Press Stop to end it early.

what_if.case: The plan says 'Not enough history'
what_if.do: It needs 28 days of sales and use. Until then, decide yourself how many to make.

what_if.case: We made the whole plan this morning
what_if.do: Open 'Record the plan in one go', untick what was not made, change what came out where it differs, press 'Record {n} batch(es)', then 'Print {n} label(s)'.

tips: The plan's 'Record these' fills in the form for you; you still check and press Record batch.
Leave 'What came out' empty when it came out as the recipe says.
Labels start at one per pan when the batch is entered in pans; you can change the number before printing.
A base recorded first is available at once for the flavours made from it; the plan in one go records bases first.
Sales use the batch with the earliest use-by first, and a batch past its use-by last.
Open a batch number to see what became of it.

screens.title: Production — What you make (batch recipes)
screens.summary: The lower part of Production: each thing the café makes in batches as a tile, opened beside the list to see its ingredients and to change it; and the form to add something new to make.
screens.get_there: Menu → Operations → Production, scroll to 'What you make'. Getting set up links straight to the add form (/production#new-recipe).

who.owner: see, add, change, stop and restart recipes
who.general_manager: the same as the owner
who.branch_manager: see the recipes and their costs Not: add or change recipes (needs recipe.edit)
who.barista: see the recipes, without costs Not: add or change recipes
who.purchasing: see the recipes and their costs Not: add or change recipes
who.accountant: see the recipes and their costs Not: add or change recipes
who.auditor: see the recipes and their costs Not: add or change recipes

what_if.case: We make a white base, then flavour it
what_if.do: Add the base first ('Something new to keep in stock'). Then add each flavour and choose the base as an ingredient, like milk or sugar.

what_if.case: The recipe changed (less sugar)
what_if.do: Open the tile, press Change…, change the line, Save changes. Batches already recorded keep what they used.

what_if.case: We stopped making a flavour
what_if.do: Open it and press 'Stop making it'. It can be brought back with 'Make it again'.

what_if.case: Gelato is kept in pans of 5 kg
what_if.do: When adding it, type 'pan' in 'Kept in a container?', holds 5 kg. Then batches can be entered in pans and labels print one per pan.

tips: About right is fine for 'One batch makes': each batch records what really came out.
Give a shelf life so every batch gets a use-by by itself.

screens.title: Batch {no}: {recipe}
screens.summary: One batch: when and by whom it was made, what came out against the recipe, its use-by, its pan labels, and what became of every bit of it, with each movement of its lot.
screens.get_there: Production → a batch number in 'Batches' or in 'In stock by batch'. Also from a batch's link elsewhere (reports).

who.owner: see the batch, print labels, change its use-by
who.general_manager: see the batch, print labels, change its use-by
who.branch_manager: see the batch, print labels, change its use-by
who.barista: see the batch and print labels Not: change the use-by
who.purchasing: see the batch and print labels Not: change the use-by
who.accountant: see the batch and print labels Not: change the use-by
who.auditor: see the batch and print labels Not: change the use-by
who.cashier: nothing Not: open it (sent to their start screen)
who.inventory_counter: nothing Not: open it (sent to their start screen)

what_if.case: A customer asks how old the gelato is
what_if.do: Open its batch: 'Made {when}' and 'To be used by {when}'.

what_if.case: The labels fell off the pans
what_if.do: Open the batch and press 'Print {n} label(s)'.

what_if.case: Some of the batch is missing
what_if.do: Look at 'Each movement of the batch'. If it was thrown away and not recorded, record a loss on Inventory, choosing this batch in 'From batch'.

tips: The lot code (B and the batch number) is printed on labels printed from this page.

screens.title: Inventory
screens.summary: What is in stock at this place, item by item, worked out from everything recorded (deliveries, sales, batches, counts, losses, transfers); the forms to change stock; and the losses waiting for a manager.
screens.get_there: Menu → Operations → Inventory. A dashboard tile for low stock also leads here.

who.owner: see the stock board and ledger, record a loss, correct stock, add items (one or a pasted list), record opening stock, approve or reverse losses waiting Not: approve a loss they recorded themselves
who.general_manager: everything the owner can except opening stock Not: record opening stock (the owner's capital); approve a loss they recorded
who.branch_manager: the same as the general manager Not: record opening stock; approve a loss they recorded
who.barista: record a loss (an item, from a batch, or a product as made); the form is open at once Not: see the stock board, costs, the ledger; correct stock; add items
who.purchasing: see the stock board and ledger, add stock items Not: record a loss, correct stock, approve losses, record opening stock
who.accountant: look at the stock board and ledger Not: change anything (no buttons are shown)
who.auditor: look at the stock board and ledger Not: change anything (no buttons are shown)
who.cashier: nothing Not: open the screen (sent to their start screen)
who.inventory_counter: nothing Not: open the screen (sent to their start screen)

what_if.case: An item shows negative stock
what_if.do: Usually a delivery was not entered: enter it on Purchasing. If the count is wrong, count it on Stock Count.

what_if.case: A loss is waiting and the barista says it did not happen
what_if.do: A manager presses Reverse…, types why, and 'Reverse the loss: the stock goes back'.

what_if.case: I recorded a loss and it waits for approval
what_if.do: Another manager approves it here or on Approvals; you cannot approve your own.

what_if.case: Which items should I order?
what_if.do: Tap 'Below reorder level', then 'What to buy →'.

tips: The tiles are filters: tap one to see only those items.
Stock is never typed in: it changes only through deliveries, sales, batches, counts, losses, corrections and transfers.

screens.title: Inventory — Record a loss
screens.summary: Recording stock that was thrown away, went off, expired, broke, melted, was lost making or preparing, or was given away (staff meal, on the house, a sample): an item (from a chosen batch) or a product as made. Over the café's limit a manager approves it with their PIN, or it waits for one.
screens.get_there: Inventory → Record a loss (open at once for a barista). Link: /inventory#record-loss.

who.owner: record a loss Not: approve their own loss later
who.general_manager: record a loss Not: approve their own loss later
who.branch_manager: record a loss Not: approve their own loss later
who.barista: record a loss Not: approve their own loss later
who.others: nothing here Not: the button is not shown

what_if.case: A latte was dropped
what_if.do: Choose Damaged (or Waste), 'A product, as made', the latte, How many 1, why. Its recipe's ingredients come out.

what_if.case: A pan of gelato expired
what_if.do: Choose Expired, the item, 'From batch' the batch, the quantity, why.

what_if.case: The staff had coffees
what_if.do: Choose Staff consumption: charged to 6110 Staff meals.

what_if.case: The loss is over the limit and no manager is here
what_if.do: Press 'Save it to wait for a manager's approval'. A manager approves it later on Inventory or Approvals.

what_if.case: I recorded the wrong quantity
what_if.do: If it is waiting, a manager reverses it and you record it again. If it was approved, a manager corrects the stock.

tips: The explanation under the kind says which account it is charged to.
Naming the batch keeps each batch's story right on its page.

screens.title: Inventory — Correct stock and Opening stock
screens.summary: A manager's correction of an item's stock outside a count, and the owner's opening stock for an item that has none yet.
screens.get_there: Inventory → 'Correct stock (manager)' or 'Opening stock'. Links: /inventory#correct-stock, /inventory#opening-stock.

who.owner: correct stock; record opening stock
who.general_manager: correct stock Not: record opening stock (owner only)
who.branch_manager: correct stock Not: record opening stock (owner only)
who.others: nothing here Not: the buttons are not shown

what_if.case: We found a box of cups not in the books
what_if.do: A manager uses Correct stock with a positive change and, if known, its cost. If a count is due, count instead.

what_if.case: Opening day: the shelves are full
what_if.do: The owner records each item's opening stock here, or pastes a list with the shelf quantities and costs (Add stock item → Paste a list).

tips: Counted stock is corrected by approving a count, not here.
The effect line shows the stock before and after before you post.

screens.title: Inventory — Add stock item (one, or paste a list)
screens.summary: Adding stock items: one at a time with its names, type, unit, pack and reorder level, or many at once pasted from Excel or Google Sheets, each row checked first.
screens.get_there: Inventory → Add stock item. Links: /inventory#add-item (one), /inventory#paste-items (paste). Products & Recipes sends here ('Add stock items') when there are no items. The same one-item form is on a delivery's line (Purchasing).

who.owner: add items, with opening stock (on the shelf, at a cost)
who.general_manager: add items Not: give opening stock (the owner's)
who.branch_manager: add items Not: give opening stock (the owner's)
who.purchasing: add items Not: give opening stock (the owner's)
who.others: nothing here Not: the button is not shown

what_if.case: Setting up the café's stock from a spreadsheet
what_if.do: Copy the rows (name, unit, reorder, shelf, cost) and paste them; fix the rows marked red; press 'Add {n} item(s)'.

what_if.case: The name looks like an existing item
what_if.do: If it is the same thing, open the existing one instead. If different, add it all the same.

tips: Pressing Add again after a dropped connection never adds an item twice.
A pack (carton of 24) lets deliveries and counts be entered in cartons.

screens.title: Stock card: {name}
screens.summary: One item's stock card: what it opened with in the dates, each kind of movement, what it closed with, every movement with the balance after it; what each delivery cost; its units; who it is bought from; and correcting the item itself (names, type, reorder and par levels, in use).
screens.get_there: Inventory → an item's name. Also from Usage (an item), a batch's page, look-alike 'Open it' links.

who.owner: read the card, add a unit, correct the item, set suppliers
who.general_manager: read the card, add a unit, correct the item, set suppliers
who.branch_manager: read the card, add a unit, correct the item, set suppliers
who.purchasing: read the card, add a unit, correct the item, set suppliers
who.accountant: read the card Not: change anything
who.auditor: read the card Not: change anything
who.barista: nothing Not: open it (sent to their start screen)
who.cashier: nothing Not: open it (sent to their start screen)
who.inventory_counter: nothing Not: open it (sent to their start screen)

what_if.case: Where did the milk go last week?
what_if.do: Set From and To to that week and Show: each kind of movement and every movement with who did it.

what_if.case: Milk now comes in crates of 12
what_if.do: Add a unit crate_12, Label 'Crate of 12', Holds 12 (in its base unit). Keep the old unit: past deliveries were in it.

what_if.case: We no longer use an item
what_if.do: Count it to 0 or record a loss, change recipes that use it, then untick 'In use' with why.

tips: The closing line is what Inventory shows at the end of the last day.
Usage links here with its own dates.

screens.title: Transfers
screens.summary: Stock sent from one of the café's places to another (the kitchen to a branch, a branch to the kitchen): sent at its cost, on its way until the other place receives it (what did not arrive is lost), or cancelled on its way.
screens.get_there: Menu → Operations → Transfers (for some roles under More). Also: Inventory → How this works → Transfers.

who.owner: send, receive and cancel transfers Not: someone set to work at one place sends from it, receives only what comes to it, and cancels only what it sent
who.general_manager: send, receive and cancel transfers Not: someone set to work at one place sends from it, receives only what comes to it, and cancels only what it sent
who.branch_manager: send, receive and cancel transfers Not: someone set to work at one place sends from it, receives only what comes to it, and cancels only what it sent
who.purchasing: send, receive and cancel transfers Not: someone set to work at one place sends from it, receives only what comes to it, and cancels only what it sent
who.accountant: see the transfers and the value on its way Not: send, receive or cancel
who.auditor: see the transfers and the value on its way Not: send, receive or cancel
who.barista: nothing Not: open it (sent to their start screen)
who.cashier: nothing Not: open it (sent to their start screen)
who.inventory_counter: nothing Not: open it (sent to their start screen)

what_if.case: The kitchen sent 10 tubs, 9 arrived
what_if.do: At the branch: 'Not all of it arrived…', type 9, a note, 'Receive what arrived'. The missing tub is written off as waste.

what_if.case: We sent it to the wrong branch
what_if.do: At the sending place, while it is on its way: 'Cancel it…', the reason, 'Cancel the transfer'. Then send it again.

what_if.case: The screen warns stock goes below zero
what_if.do: Usually a batch or a delivery was not recorded. Correct that, or 'Send it all the same' if you are sure.

tips: A batch keeps its use-by at the place it goes to.
'On its way' at the top is the value held in transit.

screens.title: Usage
screens.summary: For each item counted twice in the dates: what the counts say was used, less recorded losses, against what the recipes of what was sold and made say it should have used, and what may explain the difference.
screens.get_there: Menu → Operations → Usage (for some roles under More). Also Inventory → How this works → Usage; a Dashboard warning about usage.

who.owner: read and print it Not: change anything (it only reads)
who.general_manager: read and print it Not: change anything (it only reads)
who.branch_manager: read and print it Not: change anything (it only reads)
who.purchasing: read and print it Not: change anything (it only reads)
who.accountant: read and print it Not: change anything (it only reads)
who.auditor: read and print it Not: change anything (it only reads)

what_if.case: Milk shows +3 L difference worth 4,500 IQD
what_if.do: Open 'What it is made of'. If losses were not recorded, record them; if portions are big, train staff; count again to see the next stretch.

tips: Count the expensive items often: usage only works between two counts.

screens.title: Stock Count
screens.summary: Blind, two-person stock counts: one person counts what is on the shelf without seeing what the books expect; someone else reviews expected against counted and approves, and only then are the differences posted.
screens.get_there: Menu → Operations → Stock Count (a stock counter starts here). Also from Usage.

who.inventory_counter: start a count, enter counts, submit, cancel their own open count Not: see what is expected, review or approve
who.owner: count, review (see expected), approve or reject, cancel any open count Not: approve a count they counted (they can withdraw it for a recount)
who.general_manager: count, review (see expected), approve or reject, cancel any open count Not: approve a count they counted (they can withdraw it for a recount)
who.branch_manager: count, review (see expected), approve or reject, cancel any open count Not: approve a count they counted (they can withdraw it for a recount)

what_if.case: I forgot one item and pressed nothing yet
what_if.do: Enter its number; Submit unlocks when every item has one.

what_if.case: The count shows a big loss
what_if.do: The manager reviews; if a delivery was not entered, reject it ('recount'), enter the delivery, count again.

what_if.case: A count was started by mistake
what_if.do: Cancel this count…, reason, Cancel the count.

tips: The café can keep selling during a count: each item is compared with the stock at the moment it was counted.
Enter 0 for anything not on the shelf.

screens.title: Products & Recipes
screens.summary: The menu as tiles by the till's categories: each product's photo, price and what it costs as a share of the price. A tap opens the product beside the list, with tabs for its basics, recipe, sizes & prices and add-ons. what_if.case: A product should not be sold for a while
what_if.do: Open it, untick 'On the till', Save. Tick it again to sell it.

what_if.case: Many photos to add
what_if.do: Name each file as its product (latte.jpg) and use 'Add many at once'.

what_if.case: A tile says 'cost 120%'
what_if.do: It sells at a loss: open Sizes & prices to raise the price, or Recipe to check it.

tips: The cost share uses the cheapest size on the first channel that sells it.

what_if.case: From next Monday the latte uses 20 ml more milk
what_if.do: Change the recipe…, change the milk line, In force from next Monday, Save the new recipe. It shows under Scheduled until then.

what_if.case: A service charge has no ingredients
what_if.do: Type the reason in 'Why it uses no stock' and press 'Uses no stock'.

tips: Cups, lids and bags: set 'Takeaway & delivery' so dine-in is not charged for them.

what_if.case: Add a Large latte
what_if.do: + Add a size: name the current one Regular, the new one Large, its prices, copy Regular's recipe, Add the size; then change Large's recipe.

what_if.case: Prices go up on the 1st
what_if.do: Change a price… for each channel with From the 1st. They show under Scheduled.

what_if.case: A biscuit we buy has a barcode
what_if.do: Scan it into 'Barcode of {size}' and Save; the till adds it when scanned.

what_if.case: Cookies sold by weight
what_if.do: Tick the size under Sold by weight; price is per kilo; its recipe is for a kilo.

tips: 'Use {amount}' suggests a price for a 70% margin.
A retired size stays on old sales.

what_if.case: Latte + croissant for 5,000 in the morning
what_if.do: New deal: Thing 1 the latte, Thing 2 the croissant, prices, From 08:00 Until 11:00, Save.

what_if.case: Gelato cheaper after 21:00
what_if.do: New price by the hour: the gelato, its price, From 21:00 Until 23:59, Save.

what_if.case: A seasonal category is over
what_if.do: Untick it on the till under Categories and Save.

tips: What a deal gives away is kept as its discount in the reports.
